title: Inline R: numbers that update themselves

steps.say: A number typed into the text is right today. When the data are revised, nobody remembers to change it.
filter() finds the row and pull() takes out the number. Inline R writes it into the sentence at render time: the page reads the same, but the number is computed.
Any R expression works inline. Here: the rate in 2022 and the change since then, rounded to one decimal.
Change one line in the setup chunk and render: every number in the sentence moves with it.
Jazan's 9 and 2.1 read oddly. scales::number() fixes the format: always one decimal, and a plus sign on a rise, so 9 reads 9.0 and the change +2.1.

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
rates <- read_csv("unemployment.csv")
REGION <- "Jazan"
now <- rates |>
  filter(region == REGION, quarter == "2025Q4") |>
  pull(rate)
then <- rates |>
  filter(region == REGION, quarter == "2022Q1") |>
  pull(rate)
```

## Summary

Unemployment **fell** in most regions between 2022 and 2025.
*Jazan* is the exception. This note shows the national
trend and the latest rates.[^1]

In `r REGION` the rate was
`r scales::number(now, accuracy = 0.1)`% in 2025 Q4,
against `r scales::number(then, accuracy = 0.1)`% in
2022 Q1: a change of
`r scales::number(now - then, accuracy = 0.1, style_positive = "plus")`
points.

The data cover:

- 13 regions and the Kingdom as a whole
- 16 quarters, from 2022 Q1 to 2025 Q4

Official figures are on the [GASTAT website](https://www.stats.gov.sa).

[^1]: All figures in this note are synthetic, made for training.

## Method

The unemployment rate is

$$
u = \frac{U}{U + E} \times 100
$$

where $U$ is the number unemployed and $E$ the number employed.
